subject.title: fix: enforce sandbox tool policy for loopback tools [AI]

question: Should gateway loopback and invoke tool resolution enforce sandbox tool policy now, accepting that existing sandboxed gateway clients may lose previously exposed tools?
rationale: The patch closes a sandbox security-boundary gap through the existing policy stack, but it intentionally changes upgraded tool visibility and still lacks real runtime proof.

options.title: Require proof, then accept strict enforcement
options.body: Keep this implementation shape, but require redacted runtime loopback proof and exact-head validation before merge.

options.title: Accept upgrade risk immediately
options.body: A maintainer can intentionally accept the fail-closed behavior even if existing sandboxed clients need allowlist updates.

options.title: Pause for compatibility design
options.body: If permissive gateway behavior must remain the default, pause this PR and design an opt-in strict mode or documented migration path.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept strict enforcement
recommendation.body: Keep this implementation shape, but require redacted runtime loopback proof and exact-head validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced and refactored the gateway loopback boundary and is the best available routing owner for the security/compatibility choice.
